_comment: Hand-labelled expected assessment of data/samples/sample_security_policy.txt. Labels reflect what the document actually says, judged against the checkpoint obligations in nis2/checkpoints.py. 'must_mention' lists substrings a correct rationale should raise; they are scored separately from status so a model can be right for the wrong reason and still be caught.

NIS2-01.note: Versioned policy, approved by the Managing Director, reviewed annually.

NIS2-02.note: Risk register, annual review, scoring scale, treatment sign-off.

NIS2-03.note: Internal handling and classification exist, but nothing on notifying the CSIRT/authority or the Art. 23 24h/72h deadlines. This is the most consequential gap in the document.

NIS2-04.note: Nightly backups with retention, but no RTO/RPO, no restoration testing, and backups kept in the same building.

NIS2-05.note: 'IT services may be procured from approved vendors' imposes no security requirement and describes no supplier risk assessment.

NIS2-06.note: Nothing on secure development, change management, patching or vulnerability disclosure.

NIS2-07.note: No audit, control testing, metrics or corrective-action process.

NIS2-08.note: Onboarding briefing only: no recurring training, no completion tracking, no management-body training.

NIS2-09.note: The document contains no cryptography or encryption section whatsoever.

NIS2-10.note: No screening, employment terms, disciplinary process or leaver access revocation.

NIS2-11.note: Individual accounts and restricted admin rights, but no MFA and no periodic access review.

NIS2-12.note: No asset inventory, ownership or classification scheme.

NIS2-13.note: Office locking and keyed server room, but no visitor management and nothing environmental (power, cooling, fire).
